title: Spiralizer Recipe: Zucchini Noodle Stir‑Fry with Peanut Sauce
keyword: zucchini noodle stir fry peanut sauce
meta_description: Discover a quick, low‑carb zucchini noodle stir‑fry with peanut sauce. Learn how to use a vegetable spiralizer for perfect noodles and get tasty tips for a heal
html:
Looking for a fresh take on stir‑fry that keeps carbs low and flavor high? This zucchini noodle stir fry peanut sauce recipe swaps traditional pasta for spiralized veggies, delivering a satisfying crunch and a creamy, nutty sauce that clings to every strand. Using a vegetable spiralizer makes the prep fast and fun, and the result is a colorful bowl that feels indulgent without the guilt.

Why Spiralized Veggies Work in Stir‑Fry

Spiralized zucchini and carrots cook in minutes, so they stay crisp and retain their bright color. Because they’re thin, they absorb sauce quickly, letting the peanut sauce coat each noodle evenly. The low‑glycemic profile of zucchini also keeps blood sugar steady, making this dish a great post‑workout or weekday dinner.

Ingredients

  • 2 medium zucchinis, trimmed
  • 2 medium carrots, peeled
  • 1 cup snap peas, trimmed
  • 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or sesame oil for extra flavor)
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated
  • For the peanut sauce:
    • 3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter
    • 2 tablespoons soy sauce (or tamari)
    • 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
    • 1 teaspoon honey or maple syrup
    • ½ teaspoon chili garlic sauce (adjust to heat preference)
    • ¼ cup warm water (more if needed)
  • Fresh cilantro and chopped peanuts for garnish
  • Salt and pepper to taste

Step‑by‑Step: From Spiralizer to Plate

1. Spiralize the veggies. Using a Vegetable Spiralizer, feed the zucchini and carrots through the chosen blade. For a noodle‑like texture, select the fine‑spiral setting; a coarser setting works if you prefer a heartier bite. Set the spiraled noodles aside on a paper towel to absorb excess moisture.

2. Make the peanut sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili garlic sauce, and warm water until smooth. Adjust the thickness with a little more water if the sauce feels too thick.

3. Stir‑fry the vegetables. Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat. Add the garlic and ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant. Toss in the snap peas and red bell pepper; stir‑fry for 2‑3 minutes.

4. Combine noodles and sauce. Add the zucchini and carrot noodles to the pan. Stir constantly for 1‑2 minutes—just enough to warm the noodles without turning them soggy. Pour the peanut sauce over the vegetables, tossing to coat every strand. Cook an additional minute to let the sauce thicken slightly.

5. Finish and serve. Season with salt and pepper, then transfer to serving bowls. Sprinkle chopped peanuts and cilantro on top for crunch and freshness.

Tips for Perfect Noodles and Sauce

• Pat the zucchini noodles dry. After spiralizing, gently press the noodles with a clean kitchen towel. Removing moisture prevents a watery sauce.

• Don’t overcook. Zucchini noodles need only a quick toss; lingering too long makes them mushy.

• Adjust sauce consistency. If the peanut sauce separates, whisk in a splash of warm water or a dash of oil to bring it back together.

• Flavor boosters. A squeeze of lime juice or a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adds depth without extra effort.

Meal Prep & Variations

This dish holds up well for lunch the next day. Store the noodles and sauce separately in airtight containers; combine just before reheating to keep the noodles from soaking too much. For protein, add grilled chicken, shrimp, or tofu during step 3. If you’re not a fan of peanuts, swap the peanut butter for almond or cashew butter—just keep the same proportions.

FAQ

Can I use a regular mandoline instead of a vegetable spiralizer?

Yes, a mandoline can create thin ribbons that mimic noodles, but a dedicated vegetable spiralizer gives more consistent shape and reduces prep time.

Is this recipe gluten‑free?

It is, provided you use tamari or a gluten‑free soy sauce. All other ingredients are naturally gluten‑free.

How long will the leftover sauce stay fresh?

Store the peanut sauce in a sealed jar in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Give it a quick whisk before using again.
